Required and optional
Target labels in CSS.
The id of the control. Leave it out when the label wraps the control.
The label dims and shows a not-allowed cursor while its control is disabled, and exposes `data-required`, `data-invalid` and `data-readonly` for your own styles. It keeps up when the control changes.
The required or optional mark.
Wrap a checkbox so the whole label toggles it, or place the label beside it with htmlFor. A disabled checkbox dims its label either way.

`indicator="optional"` tags controls without `required`, and `indicator="required"` adds an asterisk to controls with it. The mark is hidden from screen readers, which already announce required fields.
